newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening flat in quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening flat in quiet day.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 20488.15 -123.41 LME CASH NICKEL US$7090 +120.0
CANDLR 1.3761 LME CASH ALUM US$1572.0 +11.5
CAN 30-YR 112.15 -0.05 BRENT CRUDE US$18.49 -0.23
* Toronto stocks were expected to open unchanged as investors await U.S. employment data due out tomorrow. * Traders said eyes were on high-techs after recent battering in New York.
Toronto stocks were expected to open flat and trade nearly unchanged on Thursday as investors await U.S. employment data due out Friday.
"I think it's going to be like yesterday, we could trade on both sides of unchanged and close basically flat," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
One trader said eyes would be on the technology sector which was battered Wednesday in New York.
"I'm watching the techs today to see what will happen to them, whether they'll continue to slide or whether they'll hold in," he said.
Languishing gold prices will likely keep the gold sector weak but refuge could be found in oil and gas, the trader said.
"I still think the oil business is the best business the country has," he said.
Beattie said the market would takes its cue from the U.S. jobs report due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Friday.
"As long as the employment report comes in as expected or weaker than expected, we should be able to get back to our all-time high," Beattie said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Index reached its record high of 6491.13 on May 26.
On Wednesday the TSE 300 slipped 4.10 points to close at 6428.62 in turnover of 99.17 million shares worth C$1.54 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped over 42 points on Wednesday.

In economic news, Canada's help wanted index, seasonally adjusted, rose four percent in May to 106 (1991=100) from 102 in April. The index was at its highest point since March 1991, Statistics Canada officials said.
